questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I am happy."

options.option_text: He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
He told that he was happy.
He says that he was happy.

questions.explanation: Present tense ('am') backshifts to past ('was'). 'I' changes to 'he'. The reporting verb 'said' stays as is (no object, so not 'told').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I will come tomorrow."

options.option_text: She said that she will come tomorrow.
She said that she will come the next day.
She said that she would come the next day.
She said that she would come tomorrow.

questions.explanation: 'Will' backshifts to 'would'. 'Tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'. Both changes are mandatory in indirect speech.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "It is raining now."

options.option_text: He said that it is raining now.
He said that it was raining then.
He said that it rained then.
He said that it was raining now.

questions.explanation: Present continuous ('is raining') backshifts to past continuous ('was raining'). 'Now' changes to 'then'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to me, "You look tired."

options.option_text: She told me that you look tired.
She said me that I looked tired.
She told me that I looked tired.
She told me that I look tired.

questions.explanation: 'Said to me' becomes 'told me'. 'You' (referring to listener = I) becomes 'I'. 'Look' backshifts to 'looked'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I went to school yesterday."

options.option_text: He said that he went to school yesterday.
He said that he had gone to school the previous day.
He said that he has gone to school the previous day.
He said that he had gone to school yesterday.

questions.explanation: Simple past ('went') backshifts to past perfect ('had gone'). 'Yesterday' changes to 'the previous day'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the imperative: The teacher said to the students, "Be quiet."

options.option_text: The teacher told the students be quiet.
The teacher said the students to be quiet.
The teacher told the students that they be quiet.
The teacher told the students to be quiet.

questions.explanation: Imperatives are reported with 'told + object + to + infinitive'. 'Said to' becomes 'told'. The 'be quiet' command becomes 'to be quiet'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I am studying for my exams."

options.option_text: She said that she is studying for her exams.
She said that she was studying for her exams.
She said that she had been studying for her exams.
She said that she studied for her exams.

questions.explanation: Present continuous ('am studying') backshifts to past continuous ('was studying'). 'My' changes to 'her'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "The earth moves around the sun."

options.option_text: He said that the earth moved around the sun.
He said that the earth was moving around the sun.
He said that the earth moves around the sun.
He said that the earth had moved around the sun.

questions.explanation: Universal truths and scientific facts do NOT undergo tense backshift in indirect speech. 'The earth moves around the sun' stays in present tense.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the negative imperative: Mother said to him, "Don't play on the road."

options.option_text: Mother told him do not play on the road.
Mother told him not to play on the road.
Mother said him not to play on the road.
Mother asked him that don't play on the road.

questions.explanation: Negative imperatives: 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Said to' becomes 'told'. The negative command becomes 'not to play'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said to her, "Are you coming with me?"

options.option_text: He asked her if she is coming with him.
He asked her whether she was coming with him.
He asked her that she was coming with him.
He asked her whether she is coming with him.

questions.explanation: Yes/No questions use 'asked...whether/if'. 'Said to' becomes 'asked'. 'You' → 'she'; 'are coming' → 'was coming'; 'me' → 'him'. Reported question has no inversion.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I have finished my work."

options.option_text: She said that she has finished her work.
She said that she finished her work.
She said that she had finished her work.
She said that she will finish her work.

questions.explanation: Present perfect ('have finished') backshifts to past perfect ('had finished'). 'My' becomes 'her'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the exclamatory: He shouted, "What a beautiful picture!"

options.option_text: He said that what a beautiful picture it was.
He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful picture.
He exclaimed with joy that it is a very beautiful picture.
He shouted that it was a beautiful picture.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences: 'exclaimed + that + it was a very + adjective + noun'. The 'What a!' structure is converted to 'it was a very...'. Tense backshifts: 'is' → 'was'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I lived here two years ago."

options.option_text: She said that she lived here two years ago.
She said that she had lived there two years before.
She said that she has lived there two years before.
She said that she lived there two years before.

questions.explanation: Simple past ('lived') → past perfect ('had lived'). 'Here' → 'there'. 'Ago' → 'before'. All three changes are mandatory.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He asked her, "What is your name?"

options.option_text: He asked her what was her name.
He asked her what her name was.
He asked her what is her name.
He told her what her name was.

questions.explanation: WH-questions: 'asked + WH word + subject + verb' (no inversion). 'What is' → 'what her name was'. The subject-verb order is uninverted in reported speech.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I can swim."

options.option_text: He said that he can swim.
He said that he might swim.
He said that he could swim.
He said that he would swim.

questions.explanation: Modal 'can' backshifts to 'could' in indirect speech. 'I' becomes 'he'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to me, "I met your brother yesterday."

options.option_text: She told me that she met my brother yesterday.
She told me that she had met my brother the previous day.
She said me that she had met my brother the day before.
She told me that she has met my brother the previous day.

questions.explanation: 'Said to me' → 'told me'. 'Met' → 'had met'. 'Yesterday' → 'the previous day'. 'Your' (referring to the listener = me) → 'my'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The doctor said to the patient, "Take this medicine twice a day."

options.option_text: The doctor told the patient that take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor told the patient take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor told the patient to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor said the patient to take this medicine twice a day.

questions.explanation: Imperative: 'told + object + to + infinitive'. 'This' → 'that' (demonstrative shift). 'Said to' → 'told'. No 'that' clause for imperatives — use infinitive directly.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I saw her when she was crossing the street."

options.option_text: He said that he saw her when she was crossing the street.
He said that he had seen her when she was crossing the street.
He said that he had seen her when she had been crossing the street.
He said that he has seen her when she was crossing the street.

questions.explanation: Main verb 'saw' → 'had seen'. The subordinate past continuous 'was crossing' typically remains unchanged as it describes ongoing background action at the time of the main event.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to him, "Will you help me?"

options.option_text: She asked him if he will help her.
She asked him whether will he help her.
She told him if he would help her.
She asked him if he would help her.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question: 'asked...if'. 'Will' → 'would'. 'You' → 'he'. 'Me' → 'her'. No inversion in reported question.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I may go abroad next year."

options.option_text: He said that he may go abroad next year.
He said that he might go abroad the following year.
He said that he might go abroad next year.
He said that he would go abroad the following year.

questions.explanation: Modal 'may' backshifts to 'might'. 'Next year' changes to 'the following year'. Both changes are required.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She told me, "I was waiting for you since morning."

options.option_text: She told me that she was waiting for me since morning.
She told me that she had been waiting for me since morning.
She told me that she has been waiting for me since morning.
She told me that she waited for me since morning.

questions.explanation: Past continuous ('was waiting') backshifts to past perfect continuous ('had been waiting'). 'You' (listener = me) → 'me'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "Honesty is the best policy."

options.option_text: She said that honesty was the best policy.
She said that honesty is the best policy.
She said that honesty has been the best policy.
She said that honesty would be the best policy.

questions.explanation: Proverbs and universal truths do NOT undergo tense backshift. 'Honesty is the best policy' remains in present tense.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the polite request: He said to her, "Please open the window."

options.option_text: He told her to please open the window.
He asked her please to open the window.
He requested her to open the window.
He requested her that she open the window.

questions.explanation: Polite requests with 'please' use 'requested + object + to + infinitive'. 'Please' is dropped from the reported form; the politeness is implied by 'requested'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I must finish this work today."

options.option_text: She said that she must finish this work today.
She said that she had to finish that work that day.
She said that she must finish that work that day.
She said that she would finish that work that day.

questions.explanation: 'Must' (obligation) changes to 'had to'. 'This' → 'that'; 'today' → 'that day'. All three changes are required simultaneously.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He asked me, "Have you ever visited Agra?"

options.option_text: He asked me if I have ever visited Agra.
He asked me if had I ever visited Agra.
He asked me if I had ever visited Agra.
He told me if I had ever visited Agra.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question: 'asked...if'. Present perfect ('have visited') → past perfect ('had visited'). No inversion in reported speech: 'if I had ever visited'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said to me, "What were you doing at noon yesterday?"

options.option_text: He asked me what I was doing at noon yesterday.
He asked me what was I doing at noon the previous day.
He asked me what I had been doing at noon the previous day.
He asked me what I have been doing at noon the previous day.

questions.explanation: WH-question: 'asked + WH word + subject + verb'. Past continuous ('were doing') → past perfect continuous ('had been doing'). 'Yesterday' → 'the previous day'. No inversion.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I wish I were a bird."

options.option_text: She said that she wished she was a bird.
She said that she wishes she were a bird.
She said that she wished she were a bird.
She said that she wished she had been a bird.

questions.explanation: The subjunctive 'were' (in 'wish' clauses) does NOT change to 'was' in reported speech — 'were' is retained. Only the reporting verb and main verb ('wish' → 'wished') change.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I shall have completed the project by Monday."

options.option_text: He said that he will have completed the project by Monday.
He said that he would complete the project by Monday.
He said that he should have completed the project by Monday.
He said that he would have completed the project by Monday.

questions.explanation: 'Shall' → 'would'. Future perfect ('shall have completed') → conditional perfect ('would have completed'). 'Monday' remains unchanged (specific day reference).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the suggestion: She said, "Let us go for a walk."

options.option_text: She said that let them go for a walk.
She told that they go for a walk.
She suggested that they should go for a walk.
She suggested that we should go for a walk.

questions.explanation: 'Let us' suggestions are reported as 'suggested that they should...'. 'We/us' → 'they' in third-person narration.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the exclamatory: He cried, "Alas! I have lost my wallet."

options.option_text: He exclaimed with joy that he had lost his wallet.
He exclaimed sorrowfully that he has lost his wallet.
He exclaimed sorrowfully that he had lost his wallet.
He cried that he lost his wallet.

questions.explanation: 'Alas!' indicates sorrow, so 'exclaimed sorrowfully'. Present perfect ('have lost') → past perfect ('had lost'). 'My' → 'his'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to him, "Please don't disturb me."

options.option_text: She told him not to disturb her.
She requested him not to disturb her.
She requested him that he should not disturb her.
She asked him please not to disturb her.

questions.explanation: Polite negative request with 'please': 'requested + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Me' → 'her'. 'Please' is dropped — 'requested' carries the polite nuance.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I had completed the assignment before she came."

options.option_text: He said that he completed the assignment before she came.
He said that he has completed the assignment before she had come.
He said that he had completed the assignment before she had come.
He said that he had completed the assignment before she came.

questions.explanation: Past perfect ('had completed') stays as past perfect — it cannot backshift further. The 'before she came' clause (simple past) also typically stays as simple past.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to me, "How long have you been waiting here?"

options.option_text: She asked me how long had I been waiting there.
She asked me how long I have been waiting here.
She asked me how long I had been waiting there.
She told me how long I had been waiting there.

questions.explanation: WH question: 'asked + how long + subject + verb' (no inversion). Present perfect continuous ('have been waiting') → past perfect continuous ('had been waiting'). 'Here' → 'there'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I would rather stay home tonight."

options.option_text: He said that he would rather stay home tonight.
He said that he rather stay home that night.
He said that he would rather stay home that night.
He said that he will rather stay home that night.

questions.explanation: 'Would rather' stays as 'would rather' (no further backshift needed as it is already past). 'Tonight' changes to 'that night'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for the military order: The general ordered the soldiers, "Attack the enemy!"

options.option_text: The general ordered the soldiers that they attack the enemy.
The general ordered the soldiers to attack the enemy.
The general told the soldiers to attack the enemy.
The general ordered the soldiers attack the enemy.

questions.explanation: Commands/orders: 'ordered + object + to + infinitive'. The reporting verb 'ordered' fits a military command more precisely than 'told'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I shall do it right now."

options.option_text: He said that he shall do it right now.
He said that he would do it right now.
He said that he should do it right then.
He said that he would do it right then.

questions.explanation: 'Shall' (for first person intention) → 'would'. 'Now' → 'then'. Both changes are required.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She asked him, "Did you lock the door before you left?"

options.option_text: She asked him if he locked the door before he left.
She asked him whether did he lock the door before he left.
She asked him if he had locked the door before he left.
She told him if he had locked the door before he left.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question: 'asked...if'. Simple past ('did lock') → past perfect ('had locked'). The subordinate past ('left') remains simple past. No inversion.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said to her, "How dare you touch my things!"

options.option_text: He asked her angrily how dare she touch his things.
He asked her angrily how she dared to touch his things.
He told her angrily that she dared touch his things.
He exclaimed that how she dared to touch his things.

questions.explanation: 'How dare you' becomes 'how she dared to'. The angry question is reported with 'asked angrily'. 'My' → 'his'. 'You' → 'she'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I've been here since last week."

options.option_text: She said that she has been here since last week.
She said that she had been here since the previous week.
She said that she had been there since the previous week.
She said that she had been there since last week.

questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been') → past perfect continuous ('had been'). 'Here' → 'there'. 'Last week' → 'the previous week'. All three changes required.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He asked her, "Will you marry me?"

options.option_text: He asked her if she will marry him.
He asked her whether would she marry him.
He asked her if she would marry him.
He told her if she would marry him.

questions.explanation: Yes/No question: 'asked...if'. 'Will' → 'would'. 'You' → 'she'. 'Me' → 'him'. No inversion in reported question.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said to his teacher, "Could you please explain this concept again?"

options.option_text: He told his teacher to explain that concept again.
He asked his teacher that could she explain that concept again.
He requested his teacher to explain that concept again.
He requested his teacher that she could explain that concept again.

questions.explanation: 'Could you please...' is a polite request: 'requested + object + to + infinitive'. 'This' → 'that'. 'Please' and 'could you' are dropped; 'requested...to' carries the meaning.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I would have called you, but I didn't have your number."

options.option_text: She said that she would have called me, but she doesn't have my number.
She said that she would call me, but she hadn't had my number.
She said that she would have called me, but she didn't have my number.
She said that she would have called me, but she hadn't my number.

questions.explanation: 'Would have called' is already in conditional perfect — no further backshift. The factual 'but' clause (simple past 'didn't have') stays in simple past. 'You' → 'me'; 'your' → 'my'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: "Let there be no noise in the hall," the teacher said.

options.option_text: The teacher said that let there be no noise in the hall.
The teacher ordered that there should be no noise in the hall.
The teacher told that there be no noise in the hall.
The teacher requested that there was no noise in the hall.

questions.explanation: 'Let there be...' (an impersonal directive) is reported as 'ordered that there should be...'. The structure 'Let there be' signals a command, not a first-person suggestion.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I wonder if she knows the truth."

options.option_text: He said that he wonders if she knows the truth.
He said that he wondered if she knew the truth.
He said that he wondered whether she knows the truth.
He said that he had wondered if she knew the truth.

questions.explanation: 'I wonder if' is a reported thought. 'Wonder' → 'wondered'. 'If she knows' → 'if she knew' (knows backshifts to knew). Both the main verb and the embedded verb change.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said, "I used to live in Mumbai before I moved here."

options.option_text: She said that she used to live in Mumbai before she moved there.
She said that she had used to live in Mumbai before she had moved there.
She said that she was used to live in Mumbai before she moved there.
She said that she used to live in Mumbai before she had moved here.

questions.explanation: 'Used to' remains 'used to' in indirect speech — it does not change form. 'Here' → 'there'. The simple past 'moved' stays as 'moved'. There is no 'had used to' form in English.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The judge said to the accused, "You may speak in your defense."

options.option_text: The judge told the accused that he may speak in his defense.
The judge told the accused that he might speak in his defense.
The judge said the accused that he might speak in his defense.
The judge told the accused that you might speak in your defense.

questions.explanation: 'May' (permission) → 'might'. 'Said to' → 'told'. 'You' → 'he'. 'Your' → 'his'. Four simultaneous changes required.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly converts: "I am feeling unwell," he said.

options.option_text: He told that he was feeling unwell.
He said that he is feeling unwell.
He said that he was feeling unwell.
He told that he is feeling unwell.

questions.explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous: 'am feeling' → 'was feeling'. 'Said' is correct (no object, so not 'told'). 'I' → 'he'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to me, "I had been trying to call you all morning."

options.option_text: She told me that she has been trying to call me all morning.
She told me that she had been trying to call me all morning.
She told me that she was trying to call me all morning.
She said me that she had been trying to call me all morning.

questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous ('had been trying') cannot backshift further — it stays as 'had been trying'. 'Said to me' → 'told me'. 'You' → 'me'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said, "I need not do it if you don't want me to."

options.option_text: He said that he doesn't need to do it if I didn't want him to.
He said that he needed not do it if I didn't want him to.
He said that he need not do it if I didn't want him to.
He said that he had not needed to do it if I didn't want him to.

questions.explanation: 'Need not' (semi-modal) retains its form in indirect speech — 'need not' stays as 'need not' (no 'needed not'). 'You don't want' → 'I didn't want'. 'Me' stays as 'him'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Direct speech: "Three years ago, I was living in Delhi," she said. Which indirect form is CORRECT?

options.option_text: She said that three years before, she had been living in Delhi.
She said that three years before, she was living in Delhi.
She said that three years ago, she had been living in Delhi.
She said that three years ago, she was living in Delhi.

questions.explanation: Two changes required: (1) 'ago' → 'before'; (2) past continuous 'was living' → past perfect continuous 'had been living'. Options B–D each miss one or both changes.
questions.subject: English
